sections.heading: 1. Key Expressions & Sentences Reviewed (Lessons 36–42)
points: Lesson 36: "Mbuya vari kurwara nhasi saka tiri kuenda kuvawona." — Grandmother is feeling unwell today, so we are going to visit her.
Lesson 37: "Mbuya vangu, avo vanogara kumusha, vanorima nzungu." — My grandmother, who lives at the rural home, grows groundnuts.
Lesson 38: "Ndapedza basa rese saka rega ndimbozorora zvishoma." — I have finished all the work, so let me rest for a little while.
Lesson 39: "Kunyangwe zvainetsa, akakwanisa kupedza chikoro." — Even though it was difficult, she managed to finish school.
Lesson 40: "Ndiri kufara nekuona shamwari dzangu dzepachikoro." — I am happy to see my friends from school.
Lesson 41: "Ndiri kunyora bvunzo dzangu dzekupedzisira svondo rino." — I am writing my final examinations this week.
Lesson 42: "Mbatya dzangu dziri panze saka ndiri kuda kudziunganidza." — My clothes are outside, so I want to gather them in.

sections.heading: 2. Core Shona Grammar Rules Consolidated
points: Actions Happening Right Now: The '-ri ku-' Progressive: [Subject + -ri] + ku-[verb] -> Ndiri kuverenga (I am reading) | Vari kufamba (They are walking) | Mvura iri kunaya (It is raining)
Present Tense & Everyday Actions ('vanogara'): [ndi- (I) / u- (you) / a- (he/she) / ti- (we) / va- (they)] + -no- + verb -> Ndinoda (I want), Vanogara (They live)
Talking About the Past ('Ndapedza'): Recent Today Past: [nda- / wa- / ta- / va-] + verb | Earlier Past: [ndaka- / waka- / taka- / vaka-] + verb
Talking About the Past ('akakwanisa'): Recent Today Past: [nda- / wa- / ta- / va-] + verb | Earlier Past: [ndaka- / waka- / taka- / vaka-] + verb

sections.heading: 3. Cultural Context & Practical Usage
points: Visiting Unwell Relatives ('Kushanyira Varwere') & Reverence for Grandmothers: In Shona culture, a grandmother ('mbuya') is revered as the matriarchal heart and storyteller of the extended family.
Groundnuts ('Nzungu'), Grinding Stones ('Guyo') & Homemade 'Dovi': Groundnuts ('nzungu') are one of the most important crops grown by grandmothers at the rural home ('kumusha').
Daily Rhythms: Early Morning Labour & Midday Rest ('Kuzorora'): In rural and peri-urban Zimbabwe, outdoor work begins at dawn when the air is cool and fresh.

Perseverance in Education ('Kupedza Chikoro') Against the Odds: Completing one's education ('kupedza chikoro') despite financial or practical hardships ('kunyangwe zvainetsa') is deeply admired across Zimbabwe, where families make immense sacrifices to see their children graduate..

review_exercises.prompt: Review 6 — Describing Clothing & Colours: How do you say 'The woman is wearing a green dress and white shoes'?
options: Murume akatenga hembe tsvuku neshangu nhema.
Musikana ane bvudzi refu nemhete chena.
Mukadzi akapfeka rokwe regirinhi neshangu chena.
Vana vakapfeka mbatya dzekuchikoro nhasi.
review_exercises.correct_answer: Mukadzi akapfeka rokwe regirinhi neshangu chena.
review_exercises.explanation: 'Akapfeka' = 'is wearing (state)', 'rokwe regirinhi' = 'a green dress', 'neshangu chena' = 'and white shoes'.

review_exercises.prompt: Review 6 — Stative Verbs ('-ka-'): Why does 'akapfeka' (using '-ka-') translate as 'is wearing' in the present?
options: Because Shona has no present tense for clothing
Because it only refers to clothes worn last year
Because '-ka-' is the future marker
With posture and clothing verbs (-pfeka, -gara, -mira), '-ka-' describes a present resulting state
review_exercises.correct_answer: With posture and clothing verbs (-pfeka, -gara, -mira), '-ka-' describes a present resulting state
review_exercises.explanation: Verbs of state like '-pfeka' (put on -> be wearing), '-gara' (sit -> be seated), and '-mira' (stand -> be standing) use '-ka-' for the current state.

review_exercises.prompt: Review 6 — Market Scenes: In 'Vakadzi vaviri vakagara pasi peamburera', where are the two women seated?
options: Underneath an umbrella
Inside a grocery shop
On top of a wooden bench
Beside a large bus
review_exercises.explanation: 'Pasi pe-' means 'underneath / below', so 'pasi peamburera' is 'under an umbrella'.

review_exercises.prompt: Review 6 — Containers & Produce: What does 'migomo miviri izere nemichero' mean?
options: three bowls of cooked vegetables
two buckets full of fruit
four bags of white maize meal
two cups of fresh milk

review_exercises.prompt: Review 6 — Traditional Delicacies: What are 'madora' in Zimbabwean cuisine?
options: Sweet pastries served with morning tea
Clay pots used for storing cool drinking water
Protein-rich mopane caterpillars, often roasted or cooked with tomatoes and onions
Woven baskets used for winnowing grain
review_exercises.correct_answer: Protein-rich mopane caterpillars, often roasted or cooked with tomatoes and onions
review_exercises.explanation: 'Madora' (mopane worms) are a prized, nutritious traditional delicacy across Zimbabwe.

review_exercises.prompt: Review 6 — Translate this new review sentence: 'Pamusika pane vanhu vazhinji vari kutenga mbatatisi nemadomasi.'
options: Inside the shop there are red shirts and black shoes.
Two girls are walking along the road carrying baskets.
My mother cooked rice and chicken for our guests.
At the market there are many people buying potatoes and tomatoes.
review_exercises.correct_answer: At the market there are many people buying potatoes and tomatoes.
review_exercises.explanation: 'Pamusika pane' = 'At the market there are', 'vanhu vazhinji vari kutenga' = 'many people buying', 'mbatatisi nemadomasi' = 'potatoes and tomatoes'.
